name: Sliding window + hash map
whenToUse: Always for this problem: values are too large for a counting array.
noC: values go up to 10⁹, so the counts need a hash map, and C has no hash map in its standard library.

card.signals: "longest subarray" (contiguous, longest) plus a rule that every window must follow ("each value at most k times"). If a window breaks the rule, any bigger window that contains it breaks it too, so you can grow on the right and shrink on the left.
card.pattern: a variable-size window. Each index enters the window once (right) and leaves at most once (left), so the whole scan is O(n). The count map holds at most n keys: O(n) space.
card.coreIdea: add nums[right]; only nums[right] can have gone over k, so move left to the right until count[nums[right]] ≤ k, then record the window length.

invariant: After each shrink loop, the window nums[left..right] is good: every value in it appears at most k times.
